messages.subject: Matching when Events are Rare
messages.body_plain:
Dear Listserve,

I am matching on a treatment variable and subsequently
looking at deaths in the sample against net use. However, after
creating a matched subset following various matching algorithms, the
number of deaths in my sample reduces significantly. I only have 100
deaths to begin with and am dubious that the analysis can be performed
on a matched subset containing 30 or fewer deaths. Is there anyway to
retain the deaths in matching, or is that simply not possible,
analogous to matching on outcomes?

Sincerely,

Andy Stokes
Institute for Health Metrics & Evaluation

messages.subject: Re: Matching when Events are Rare
messages.body_plain:
well, this is potentially 'good' news in the sense that now you know 
this and you didn't do something bad, like some type of extrapolation 
that regression would do (but more or less hide)

what this is saying (to me) is that your deaths group differs quite 
significantly from the comparison group--so that's good to know

i guess i would do three things;
- make sure you didn't make a mistake in model specification so that 
this is an error
- try a couple of different matching schemes just to make sure the 
finding is robust
- try to look more carefully at what's driving the difference -- look at 
the model that's generating the propensity score
are there coefficients that are enormous?

/michael

I agree with these suggestions. If you are doing one-to-one matching, then 
you could try one-to-n (with n > 1) matching to see if you can increase 
the sample size without worsening balance.
